South Korea, officially the Republic of Korea (ROK), is the state in the southern half of the Korean Peninsula, founded in 1948 with Seoul as its capital. The chart's bar is North and South Korea.

It began in the American zone south of the 38th parallel, under President Syngman Rhee. The North's invasion in 1950 began the Korean War, which left the country ruined and divided by a ceasefire line in 1953.

The next decades were authoritarian and fast-growing:

  • 1960: student protests toppled Rhee.
  • 1961: General Park Chung Hee seized power and drove export-led industry, built around big family firms such as Samsung.
  • 1980: troops crushed the Gwangju Uprising, killing hundreds.
  • 1987: mass protests won direct presidential elections.

Seoul hosted the 1988 Olympics. Since then South Korea has been a democracy and one of the richest countries in Asia, known for its electronics, cars and ships and for its films, dramas and pop music. It still faces North Korea across one of the most heavily fortified borders in the world.
